Issued at 310 AM EDT Sat Aug 22 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Ridge axis stretches from British Columbia down to the Four Corners 
region, where the 598/599dm upper level heat dome remains in 
place...with an upper low just off the West Coast poised to try to 
eject northward. Meanwhile, downstream, NW flow overtaking the 
Central US, with sharp trough axis focused from KY northward through 
MI into central Ontario...and another shortwave trough dropping out 
of Manitoba as of 3z. Shortwave ridge axis over eastern Canada as 
upper troughing exits the Canadian coast. Bulk of the moisture 
across the continent is focused along the SE US coast along a 
boundary stretching loosely down the Atlantic coast and through the 
Gulf Coast states...and secondly, across the Upper Great Lakes up 
into Hudson Bay near/beneath the incoming troughing. Anticyclonic 
flow in the low/mid-levels over central Canada helping to reinforce 
cold northwesterly flow across Manitoba and western Ontario, where 
850mb temps are in the 4-8C range attm...and a surface cold front 
stretching from MN to Hudson Bay reflects this cold advection idea. 
A cold front does stretch from the central UP down into the Mid MS 
Valley and Central Plains, though for our neck of the woods, the 
thermal change is less impressive than the wind shift attm, with 
winds distinctly turning around to the NW behind it (as opposed to 
the southerly surface flow ahead of it). 

Expect this latter feature will be exiting NE MI this morning as 
that energy digs nearly straight south from northwestern Ontario. 
This should keep the threat for showers and perhaps storms going 
through the day as multiple waves dig through the region. 
Strengthening pressure gradient between departing pressure falls and 
approaching surface high will result in strengthening northwest 
winds later today into tonight...and hanging on into Sunday as an 
somewhat unseasonable wad of PV drops in and results in a 
strengthening of aforementioned pressure falls to our E/NE. Falling 
temps aloft should generate overlake instability and lake effect 
rain showers to wrap up the weekend. Not impossible this idea hangs 
on into the start of the workweek, but attm, appears ridging should 
build eastward into the Upper Midwest later Monday...ahead of the 
next feature plowing its way across southern Canada...which should 
reach us by midweek, though its warm advective influences may reach 
us a tad sooner. It is still somewhat unclear attm how the end of 
next week will evolve, though signals the last few nights suggest 
the flow may try to flatten out across the northern CONUS as bits of 
energy continue to track across Canada. 

FORECAST DETAILS...

Rain/storm chances today through Sunday (Monday?)... 

Think there is a reasonable shot at a PV max lifting through around 
midday/afternoon today, and another, more potent bit of PV digging 
in from the northwest toward late afternoon/evening...perhaps not 
all that dissimilar to yesterday's setup, but translated eastward a 
bit...though certainly possible there will be other, smaller-scale 
perturbations to contend with. We will continue to hang onto several 
hundred to around 1000 joules of elevated instability this morning, 
and think this could have a shot at becoming surface based with time 
today, especially toward NE Lower which should remain in the warm 
sector longest...though if we are able to warm enough to mix out any 
weak nocturnal inversion this morning, we could become surface based 
right away with low-LCLs, and do wonder (with my very worst-case-
scenario brain) if a rogue spin-up is possible?...though shear 
generally remains weak till perhaps the afternoon (and even at that, 
is likely marginal, around 20-30kts at best)...though I am perhaps a 
bit aggressively biased toward the idea of lifting/negatively tilted 
shortwaves tending to be spicy. Some upscale growth is possible with 
shear vectors largely parallel to the boundary, and cooling/weak 
stability aloft suggests some marginal hail could be possible...but 
some localized heavy rains could also be a concern, especially if 
storms move slowly or hang out in an area for an extended time. 

925mb temps falling below 14C as early as 3z tonight suggest we will 
begin to transition to more of a lake effect regime, and this should 
remain firmly in place Sunday as temps fall even further -- 850mb 
temps could fall below 4C, which would be sufficient to generate 
overlake instability over even the colder waters of central Lake 
Superior. Prevailing flow should generally be NW to NNW but may 
fluctuate back and forth a bit with the encroaching perturbations, 
with more northerly flow likely by later Sunday into Sunday night. 
Deepest moisture should remain over NE Lower MI Sunday, and this is 
where best coverage should be...though will expect most of the usual 
lake effect areas to see a little activity off and on this weekend.
